title: Town office space
question: What would consolidating town offices cost compared with renovating Town Hall and Ritter?

answers.text:
Review of the first draft. Its headline claim is wrong and must not ship; rule 13c applies.

1. THE PLAN IS PRICED, IN THE ARCHIVE. sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/fy26-budget/parks-and-town-hall-presentations/2025-lmbdc-taylor-burns-design.pdf (sha256 in sources/budget-workbooks/index.csv), page 40, "COST ESTIMATE": Meeting House Renovation, Ritter Memorial Renovation, Town Hall (new), Sitework, subtotals, and "Total Project Cost w/ OPM & Design Fees" as a range; alternates priced separately. Its text extract (text/2025-lmbdc-taylor-burns-design.pdf.txt) holds that page. Read every line of the page off the document and cite it. Pages 6-11 carry the square footage per room. The PDF is MIXED (scripts/pdf_kind.py): 21 of 40 pages are pictures, so say which pages you could not read rather than calling anything absent. Search the rest of the archive for the thing (municipal building, Taylor, Ritter, Meeting House), not for one pattern.

2. LEAD WITH THE 2025 PLAN AND WHAT HAPPENED TO IT. The October 2022 concepts are history, not the answer. The Finance Committee's own minutes of 2025-05-08 (sources/meetings/text/finance-committee/2025-05-08-minutes-7210.txt) record "the vote against recommendation". Our minutes of the committee on 2025-06-05 (sources/data/recording-minutes/lunenburg-municipal-building-design-committee/) describe it falling short of two-thirds at Town Meeting and losing at the ballot -- that is a caption-derived record, so label it as ours, and look for the town's own Town Meeting / election record before stating the outcome as fact. If the town's record cannot be found, say which documents were searched.

3. WHERE IT STANDS NOW, from the committee's 2026 meetings in recording-minutes: offices only, no school departments (2026-08-17); Ritter too small, needs an addition (2026-08-31); a square-footage-and-cost RFP, no November article (2026-10-05). The Select Board on 2026-10-06 questioned whether consolidating offices should drive the project. Cite each to the video second.

4. The question is "consolidate vs renovate". The 2025 plan WAS consolidation (renovate Meeting House and Ritter, build a new Town Hall addition). Compare it to the current direction and to the capital-plan repair lines only where like is compared with like (rule 1 / rule 13a: a consultant estimate is not a budget and not an actual; say which each figure is).

5. Remove or correct the three money-gaps rows you added: the first two claim the archive holds no price. Keep only gaps that remain true after reading page 40, each with its "-- closes:" document.

6. There is now a thread, id town-offices, in the person's tree (/Users/tj/lunenburgbudgets/sources/data/threads.csv, read-only to you); it is not on your branch. Do not edit threads.csv; name the thread in your result so it can be linked at publish.

result.summary: Rebuilt /town-office-space around the 2025 plan. It prices the plan from page 40 of the Taylor & Burns deck ($21,409,100 to $22,301,145), shows it falling 7 votes short of two-thirds at Town Meeting and losing the 17 May 2025 ballot, 553 to 174 (from the town's FY2025 annual report), and then covers the committee's 2026 direction, which has no price yet. The wrong "no price exists" claim is gone, and the money-gaps rows are replaced with four that stay true after reading page 40. Thread to link at publish: town-offices.

reasons: Every figure on the estimate, vote, current-direction and upkeep pages is read from files and asserted by the generator. The page-40 trade costs must add to the printed subtotal, the ballot precincts to the totals, and each quoted minute must be verbatim.

Four things need a person. First, the ballot result sits in a printed text layer, and Article 29's Town Meeting tally is printed under the heading 'Article 28'; we read it as Article 29's and a person should confirm that against the Town Clerk's tally.

Second, the 2026 direction is partly caption-derived (the offices-only decision, the 5 October 'no dollar figure', the Select Board's 6 October remark). Those are cited to the video second and labelled ours, and a person must check them at the second.
Third, the headline question, consolidate versus renovate in dollars, cannot be answered by a script. The current direction has no estimate until the committee's RFP returns.
Fourth, 21 of the deck's 40 pages are pictures that were not read, and the architects' report dated 24 February 2025 is not in the archive.
